newsitem.title: UK: UK stocks weaken as rate, currency woes weigh.
newsitem.headline: UK stocks weaken as rate, currency woes weigh.

text.p: UK shares ushered in the new month with a 0.5 percent drop as investors fretted over the strength in sterling and rising interest rates, yet many traders and strategists said they still hold out hope for a year end rally.

The leading FTSE 100 ended 19.5 points lower at 4,038.5, as decliners beat advancers by a margin of about two to one. Second-liners fared a bit better. The FTSE 250 lost 13.7 points to settle at 4,414.8. Volume was thin, with only 463.1 million shares recorded by 1636 GMT.
"I do think we'll see a year end rally. Equities look very attractive relative to bonds," said Tim Russell head of UK equities at Lazard Investors. "The only caveat is Wall Street."
UK shares sank to the day's low as the Dow stumbled by almost 50 points after U.S. economic indicators pointed to robust activity in the manufacturing and construction sectors.

Jitters that the U.S. stock market -- up a staggering 20 percent since late July --- is poised for a correction, plus growing expectations that UK interest rates are headed higher means any advance is likely to be an uphill battle, traders said.
They said the December 11 UK monetary meeting could see a hike in interest rates, after reports of rising house prices and a decision by Abbey National to raise mortgage rates.
But with institutions still flush with cash as the year draws to a close, a decline in UK shares is likely to be met with fresh buying, said one trader.
"I can't see the market coming back too far," he said. "I think we'll see 4,200 or 4,250 before we see 4,000 again."
BZW equity strategist Steve Wright wasn't convinced. He said he expects the UK shares to remain flat to lower amid more currency-related earnings downgrades.
Companies hit hardest by currency considerations will be those with a large proporation of overseas business, like Unilever, Glaxo Wellcome, SmithKline Beecham, and Shell Transport.
Shares in Abbey National and Lloyds TSB climbed after Abbey's move to raise mortgage rates. Abbey shares gained 12p to 708-1/2, while Lloyds climbed 8p to 420-1/2p.
Among non-FTSE 100 stocks, shares in Racal Electronics tumbled 50-1/2p, or more than 18 percent, to 224-1/2p after the company issued a profit warning.
Shares in Scottish & Newcastle added 21-1/2p to 660-1/2p, after the UK brewer reported strong interim results, prompting an upgrade from brokerage UBS.
